newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan says not preparing to seek court protection.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan says not preparing to seek court protection.

text.p: Yaohan Japan Corp said on Thursday that it was not preparing to seek court protection from creditors.

Yaohan Japan president Mitsumasa Wada made those remarks during a hastily called news conference after the Yomiuri Shimbun newspaper's wire service reported on Thursday that the retailer is in talks with financial institutions on possible changes in its restructuring plan.
The report said the company may be forced to apply for court mediation.
Earlier on Thursday, the supermarket chain operator said it was not considering applying to the court for an arrangement with creditors under Japanese bankruptcy laws.

On the Tokyo bourse, Yaohan was the largest percentage loser on Thursday, falling 17 yen to end at 143 yen. The retailer's shares hit a record low of 133 yen in intraday trade on Wednesday before recovering to close at 160.
"I've never dreamed of seeking court mediation from creditors, or been prepared for it," Wada said.

The president said he was not considering holding talks with creditor banks, but said that it was true that his company had requested some of its suppliers accept a delay in payments worth some 5.5 billion yen.
